topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how known immune components combine into coordinated reactions.

topics.label: Innate Immune Sensing: PAMPs, DAMPs, and Non-Self Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how the innate immune system detects infection and cellular damage through molecular patterns that distinguish foreign pathogens from self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptors and Signaling Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic encoding, subcellular distribution, and downstream activation cascades of the cellular receptor families and multi-protein complexes that transduce danger signals.

topics.label: Inflammatory Activation, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells initiate immune defenses, orchestrate the extravasation and migration of circulating leukocytes into tissues, and cause systemic complications when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Pathologies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system dampens acute inflammation, coordinates tissue rebuilding, and transitions into chronic inflammation or containment structures when pathogens cannot be cleared.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
